nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $b_n$ be $1$ if the computable decoder returns an oracle code on $n$, and $0$ otherwise. For every natural number $m$, the one-step function of the course-of-values recursion for definedness, applied to the list $(b_0, b_1, \dots, b_{m-1})$, returns $b_m$.
nodes.title: The definedness step function is correct

The step takes an argument of the unit type, which it ignores, and a list $L$ of natural numbers; for $i \in \mathbb{N}$ write $L_i$ for the entry of $L$ at position $i$ (counting from $0$), with $L_i = 0$ when $i$ is at least the length of $L$. nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the Boolean value that is true exactly when the computable decoder of oracle codes returns an oracle code on $n$.
nodes.title: Whether a code number decodes

nodes.summary: For every oracle code $c$, the computable decoder applied to the Gödel number of $c$ returns $c$.
nodes.title: The computable decoder inverts the encoder

nodes.summary: Write $\langle a, b \rangle$ for the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of the Gödel numbering. Let $c$ be an oracle code with Gödel number $\langle t, p \rangle$. For every fuel $f$ strictly greater than the depth of $c$, the fuel-indexed decoder with fuel $f$, tag $t$ and payload $p$ returns $c$.
nodes.title: The fuel-indexed decoder inverts the encoder

nodes.summary: The fuel-indexed decoder agrees with the total decoder whenever the code number is below the fuel: decoding `(tag, payload)` at any fuel above the code number gives the same result as decoding the code number itself.
nodes.title: The fuel-indexed decoder agrees with the total decoder

nodes.summary: Write $\langle a, b \rangle$ for the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of the Gödel numbering. For every fuel $f$, tag $t$, payload $p$ and oracle code $c$, if the fuel-indexed decoder with fuel $f$, tag $t$ and payload $p$ returns $c$, then the Gödel number of $c$ is $\langle t, p \rangle$.
nodes.title: Decoder soundness

nodes.summary: Write $\langle a, b \rangle$ for the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of the Gödel numbering. Given a fuel $f$, a tag $t$ and a payload $p$, the decoder either returns an oracle code or fails; to decode a number $n = \langle n_1, n_2 \rangle$ with fuel $f$ means to run it with fuel $f$, tag $n_1$ and payload $n_2$. With fuel $0$ it fails. With fuel $f + 1$, writing…

Then for all natural numbers $t$ and $p$, the value $\mathrm{dec}\langle t, p \rangle$ is: $\mathsf{zero}$,…
nodes.title: The decoder, by cases on the tag

nodes.summary: The computable decoder for the Gödel numbering of oracle codes sends a natural number $n$ to the result of the fuel-indexed decoder with fuel $n + 1$, tag $n_1$ and payload $n_2$, where $(n_1, n_2)$ is the unpairing of $n$; the result is either an oracle code or undefined. The fuel $n + 1$ is more than enough, since the depth of an oracle code is at most its code number.
nodes.title: Decoding oracle codes

nodes.summary: The Gödel numbering of oracle codes is injective.
nodes.title: The Gödel numbering of oracle codes is injective

nodes.summary: Write $\langle a, b \rangle$ for the pairing of natural numbers equal to $b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and to $a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. The code number $\ulcorner c \urcorner$ of an oracle code $c$ is defined by recursion on $c$: $\mathsf{zero}$, $\mathsf{succ}$, $\mathsf{left}$, $\mathsf{right}$ and $\mathsf{oracle}$ have code numbers $\langle 0, 0 \rangle$, $\langle 1, 0 \rangle$, $\langle 2, 0 \rangle$,…
nodes.title: The Gödel numbering of oracle codes

nodes.summary: For a predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$, the Turing jump $P'$ is the predicate that holds at $n$ exactly when the $n$-th oracle code in the effective enumeration of oracle codes, evaluated with the oracle that answers $1$ at $m$ if $P(m)$ holds and $0$ otherwise, halts on input $n$. Thus $P'$ is the diagonal halting set of the universal oracle machine with oracle $P$.
nodes.title: The Turing jump

nodes.summary: The function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ sending $n$ to $1$ if $n$ decodes to an oracle code under the computable decoder and to $0$ otherwise is primitive recursive.
nodes.title: The definedness predicate is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: For every oracle code $c$, the depth of $c$ is at most the code number of $c$ under the Gödel numbering of oracle codes.
nodes.title: Depth is bounded by the code number

nodes.summary: Leaves have depth `0`; each constructor adds one to the maximum depth of its children.
nodes.title: Depth of an oracle code

nodes.summary: For every oracle code $c$, the effective enumeration of oracle codes sends the code number of $c$ to $c$.
nodes.title: The effective enumeration is a left inverse of the Gödel numbering

nodes.summary: The enumeration of oracle codes is surjective.
nodes.title: The enumeration of oracle codes is surjective

nodes.summary: The $n$-th oracle code is the code that the computable decoder of the Gödel numbering of oracle codes assigns to $n$, or the basic code $\mathtt{zero}$ (the constant $0$ program) when $n$ is not the number of any code. Because the decoder inverts the Gödel numbering, this is an effective enumeration tied to that numbering, not an arbitrary countable encoding.
nodes.title: Effective enumeration of oracle codes

nodes.summary: Oracle codes are the finite programs built from the basic codes $\mathtt{zero}$, $\mathtt{succ}$, $\mathtt{left}$, $\mathtt{right}$ and $\mathtt{oracle}$ by the binary constructors $\mathtt{pair}$, $\mathtt{comp}$ and $\mathtt{prec}$ and the unary constructor $\mathtt{rfind}$. They are the codes for partial recursive functions (constant zero, successor, the two unpairing projections, pairing, composition, primitive…
nodes.title: Oracle codes

nodes.summary: Let $o$ be an oracle that assigns to each natural number either a natural number or no value, $c$ an oracle code and $n$ a natural number. The value of $c$ on $n$ relative to $o$ is the value returned by the fuel-indexed evaluator of $c$ on $n$ relative to $o$ at the least fuel $k$ for which that evaluator returns a value; it is undefined when there is no such $k$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of oracle codes

nodes.summary: For every oracle $o$, fuel $k$, oracle code $c$ and input $n$, if the fuel-indexed evaluator with fuel $k$ returns a value on $c$ and $n$ relative to $o$, then $n < k$.
nodes.title: Fuel bounds the inputs

nodes.summary: Write $\langle a, b \rangle$ for the pairing of natural numbers. For an oracle $o$ assigning to each natural number a natural number or no value, a fuel $k$, an oracle code $c$ and an input $n$, the evaluator $E_k(c, n)$ returns a natural number or fails. $E_0(c, n)$ always fails. $E_{k+1}(c, n)$ fails if $n > k$; otherwise, with $n = \langle a, m \rangle$:
nodes.title: Fuel-indexed evaluation of oracle codes

nodes.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing of natural numbers, equal to $b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and to $a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. For every natural number $x$, $x < \langle 4, x \rangle$.
nodes.title: Pairing with $4$ strictly increases the second argument

nodes.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing of natural numbers, equal to $b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and to $a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. For all natural numbers $a$ and $b$, $a \le \langle a, b \rangle$.
nodes.title: Pairing is at least its first argument

nodes.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing of natural numbers, equal to $b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and to $a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. For all natural numbers $a$ and $b$, $b \le \langle a, b \rangle$.
nodes.title: Pairing is at least its second argument

nodes.summary: Let $\langle a, b \rangle$ denote the pairing of natural numbers, equal to $b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and to $a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. For all natural numbers $t$ and $x$ with $t \ge 1$, $x < \langle t, x \rangle$.
nodes.title: Pairing with a positive first argument strictly increases the second

nodes.summary: One step of the course-of-values recursion for definedness is primitive recursive as a function of its two arguments, an element of the unit type and a list of natural numbers.
nodes.title: The course-of-values step for definedness is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: Regard oracle codes as coded by their Gödel numbers. Then the computable decoder, which sends a natural number $n$ to the oracle code with Gödel number $n$ when there is one and to no value otherwise, is primitive recursive as a map from natural numbers to optional oracle codes.
nodes.title: The Gödel decoder of oracle codes is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: Regard oracle codes as coded by their Gödel numbers, with the computable decoder as decoding. Then the map sending each oracle code to its Gödel number is primitive recursive.
nodes.title: The Gödel encoding of oracle codes is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: Regard oracle codes as coded by their Gödel numbers. Then the effective enumeration of oracle codes, which sends a natural number $n$ to the oracle code with Gödel number $n$ when there is one and to the zero code otherwise, is primitive recursive.
nodes.title: The effective enumeration of oracle codes is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: The Turing degree of a predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is the Turing degree of its characteristic function, that is, the class of the characteristic function of $P$ under Turing equivalence of partial functions $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Turing degree of a predicate

nodes.summary: Two predicates $P$ and $Q$ on the natural numbers are Turing equivalent when the characteristic function of $P$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $Q$ and the characteristic function of $Q$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $P$.
nodes.title: Turing equivalence of predicates

nodes.summary: Every predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is Turing reducible to itself.
nodes.title: Turing reducibility is reflexive

nodes.summary: For predicates $P$, $Q$ and $R$ on the natural numbers, if $P$ is Turing reducible to $Q$ and $Q$ is Turing reducible to $R$, then $P$ is Turing reducible to $R$.
nodes.title: Turing reducibility is transitive

nodes.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is Turing reducible to a predicate $Q$ on the natural numbers when the characteristic function of $P$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $Q$, that is, partial recursive relative to an oracle for the characteristic function of $Q$.
nodes.title: Turing reducibility of predicates

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pair} : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be the pairing bijection with $\mathrm{pair}(a, b) = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\mathrm{pair}(a, b) = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. For every natural number $n$, the first component of $\mathrm{pair}^{-1}(n)$ is at most $n$.
nodes.title: The first unpairing component is at most the number

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pair} : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be the pairing bijection with $\mathrm{pair}(a, b) = b^2 + a$ if $a < b$ and $\mathrm{pair}(a, b) = a^2 + a + b$ otherwise. For every natural number $n$, the second component of $\mathrm{pair}^{-1}(n)$ is at most $n$.
nodes.title: The second unpairing component is at most the number

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
